newsitem.title: USA: Foundation, Health Systems gain in size.
newsitem.headline: Foundation, Health Systems gain in size.

text.p: The merger between Foundation Health Corp and Health Systems International Inc on Tuesday gives the combined company the size to do battle with rival health maintenance firms in the huge California market.

The two were in danger of being left behind in August after PacifiCare Health Systems Inc and FHP International Corp said they were creating the country's fifth largest managed care company in a $2.1 billion deal.
"I'm sure they wanted to maintain a competitive position," said Piper Jaffray analyst Russell Johnson. "I'm sure that was a factor in bringing the two companies together."

Foundation Health and Health Systems said they signed a definitive agreement to combine in a merger of equals. The deal is valued at about $3.0 billion, based on the companies' combined market capitalization, the companies said.
The two were reported in September to be in merger talks.
U.S. health maintenance organizations have been in a wave of mergers in an effort to drive down costs and better compete for contracts among employers and other healthcare buyers.
Analysts said potential cost savings in the merger were not huge, at about $150 million a year and mainly in corporate overhead rather than medical cost savings.
They said a major gain in the merger would be the combined company's ability to offer buyers a health plan with a large geographic network.

Foundation Health's core business is in California's Sacramento valley, but it lacked strength outside that region, which it will gain from Health Systems, analysts said. The merger gives Health Systems a presence in the Sacramento area.

"This delivers (Health Systems) a stronghold in Sacramento," said Chicago Corp's Peter Costa. "Foundation was a little stuck on where it could get growth going in the future...it need something to boost it up again."

The merged company will also have presence in Western states, including Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico and Oregon, giving it geographic breadth the companies lacked individually. This improves their position with buyers seeking healthcare providers with broad networks, analysts said.
"It makes them a stronger player with the national accounts," said Mary O'Connell of Josephthal, Lyon and Ross.
